instructions: Slice or shred 2 cups of leftover roast chicken into bite-size pieces. Toss it in a bowl with 1/4 cup of the pesto.
Lay out 8 slices of the sourdough and spread 1 tbsp pesto over one side of each, 1/2 cup in all.
Drain 1/2 cup of the sun-dried tomatoes and pat them dry on paper towel.
On 4 of the slices, pesto side up, divide the chicken, then the 8 oz mozzarella, the sun-dried tomatoes and 2 cups of the spinach. Top with the other 4 slices, pesto side down.
Brush the outsides of the sandwiches with the 2 tbsp olive oil.

Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium for 2 minutes. Put in 2 of the sandwiches and set a heavy pan on top to press them down. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp.

Flip them, put the heavy pan back on and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's golden and the cheese is melting out at the edges. If the bread browns before the cheese melts, turn the heat down a little.
Cook the other 2 sandwiches the same way. If you have a panini press, cook them in it for about 5 minutes instead.
Cut them in half and serve hot.
method_notes: Both read versions put chicken, pesto and mozzarella between slices of bread and press the sandwich in a hot pan until the bread is crisp and the cheese melts. Tasting Table (the lead) coats the chicken in pesto, spreads more pesto on the sourdough, adds sun-dried tomatoes and spinach, and presses the sandwiches under a heavy skillet or in a panini press for 3 to 4 minutes a side. Kitchen Swagger sears thin raw chicken breasts first, uses fresh mozzarella, tomato and balsamic glaze on panini bread, and presses the sandwich with a spatula in the same pan. This one follows the lead but starts from leftover roast chicken.
